chapters.name: Compass navigation
chapters.blurb: Take and follow a bearing with a lensatic compass, find where you are, and map an area by pacing.
checks: Name the parts of a lensatic compass and say what each one does.
Take a bearing to a landmark and read it within 2° of a partner's reading.
Set a bearing on the bezel ring by counting clicks, and follow it to a marker at least 100 m away.
Convert a magnetic bearing to a true bearing for your area, and work out its back bearing.
Know your pace count for 100 metres on flat ground.
Find your position on a map from bearings to two or more landmarks.
Survey a campsite by compass and pacing, and draw it with a north arrow and scale bar.

chapters.name: Reading a topographic map
chapters.blurb: Scale, symbols and contour lines: read the shape of the land before you walk it.
checks: Explain what a map's scale means, and measure a route's length on the map.
Name what the main map colours show.
Point out a hill, valley, ridge, saddle and steep slope from the contour lines alone.
Give a six-figure grid reference for a point, and find a point from one.
Orient a map with a compass so that it lines up with the land.
Plan a day route and estimate how long it will take.

chapters.name: The Ten Essentials and trip planning
chapters.blurb: What to carry on every outing, what to leave with someone at home, and how to keep water safe.
checks: Pack the Ten Essentials for a day hike and explain why each one is there.
Write a trip plan and leave it with a responsible adult.
Choose clothing layers for the forecast, without relying on cotton.
Make water safe to drink by boiling, filtering or chemical treatment.

chapters.name: Knots and rope
chapters.blurb: Seven knots that cover nearly every job in camp, with what each is for and how to tie it.
checks: Tie a square knot and say when not to use it.
Tie a bowline around your own waist.
Tie two half hitches and a clove hitch around a post.
Tie a taut-line hitch on a tent guy line and adjust it.
Join two ropes of different thickness with a sheet bend.
Tie a timber hitch and use it to drag a log.
Whip or seal the end of a rope, and coil it for storage.

chapters.name: Camping and Leave No Trace
chapters.blurb: Pick a safe site, store food, handle fire and stoves, and leave the place better than you found it.
checks: Choose a tent site and explain why it is safe and durable.
Name the seven Leave No Trace principles and give an example of each.
Light, manage and fully put out a fire where fires are allowed.
Use a camp stove safely, including refuelling.
Store food and scented items so that animals cannot get them.
Dig a cathole the right depth and distance from water.

chapters.name: First aid in the field
chapters.blurb: A refresher for the problems scouts meet most outdoors. It is not a replacement for a course.
checks: Explain the first steps at any emergency: scene, person, call, care.
Show how to control bleeding with direct pressure.
Treat a minor burn and a blister.
Recognise heat exhaustion, heat stroke and hypothermia, and say what to do for each.
Remove a tick correctly.
Pack a group first-aid kit and say what each item is for.
